A First Analysis in Four Calls

Source: vignettes/first-analysis.qmd

Overview

mediationverse does not define its own mediate() function. The entry point already exists upstream: medfit::med() takes a data frame and three variable names and returns a fitted mediation object. The other packages then work on that same object.

This article runs one complete analysis in four calls:

  1. Simulate data (or bring your own).
  2. Fit the model with medfit::med().
  3. Get a confidence interval for the indirect effect with RMediation.
  4. Get the effect size Pmed with probmed.

medfit is attached with library(mediationverse); the code below calls it with medfit:: so it runs the same either way. RMediation and probmed are optional, so each of their calls is guarded and is skipped when the package is not installed.

Call 1: data

A binary treatment A, a mediator M, an outcome Y and one covariate C. The true indirect effect is 0.5 x 0.4 = 0.2.

set.seed(1)
n <- 300
A <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)
C <- rnorm(n)
M <- 0.5 * A + 0.3 * C + rnorm(n)
Y <- 0.4 * M + 0.2 * A + 0.1 * C + rnorm(n)
dat <- data.frame(A, M, Y, C)

Call 2: fit 

fit <- medfit::med(
  dat,
  treatment = "A",
  mediator = "M",
  outcome = "Y",
  covariates = "C"
)
fit
MediationData object
====================

Path coefficients:
  a (X -> M):        0.4755
  b (M -> Y|X):      0.4355
  c' (X -> Y|M):     0.2472
  Indirect (a*b):    0.2071

Variables:
  Treatment: A
  Mediator:  M
  Outcome:   Y

Model info:
  N observations: 300
  Converged:      Yes
  Source:         stats::glm

Residual SDs:
  Mediator model:   1.0879
  Outcome model:    1.0485

Extractors return single effects: medfit::nie(fit) (natural indirect), medfit::nde(fit) (natural direct), medfit::te(fit) (total) and medfit::pm(fit) (proportion mediated). For bootstrap inference add boot = TRUE, n_boot = 1000, seed = 123 to the call.

Call 3: confidence interval for the indirect effect

RMediation::ci_mediation_data() accepts the fitted object directly and uses the distribution of the product by default.

if (requireNamespace("RMediation", quietly = TRUE)) {
  RMediation::ci_mediation_data(fit, level = 0.95)
}
$CI
[1] 0.09453522 0.33518940

$Estimate
[1] 0.2070642

$SE
[1] 0.06140013

Call 4: effect size

probmed::pmed() also accepts the fitted object. Pmed is the probability that the mediator shift leaves a random individual better off.

if (requireNamespace("probmed", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(2)
  probmed::pmed(fit)
}

P_med: Probability of Mediated Shift
====================================

Estimate: 0.55
95% CI: [ 0.519 ,  0.58 ]

Indirect Effect (Product of Coefficients):
Estimate: 0.205
95% CI: [ 0.0898 ,  0.33 ]

Inference: parametric_bootstrap
Bootstrap samples: 1000

Treatment contrast: X = 1 vs. X* = 0

Interpretation:
  P(Y(1, M(1)) > Y(1, M(0))) = 0.55
  P that the mediator shift (M(0) -> M(1)) leaves a random individual better off, holding X = 1.

Where to go next

  • mediationverse_sitrep() shows which of these packages are installed and current; mediationverse_news() shows what changed in each.
  • vignette("mediationverse-workflow") extends this to sensitivity analysis and simulation.
  • Assumptions (sequential ignorability, positivity, consistency) still apply; none of the four calls checks them.
